findings.title: Early return on date override skips busy-time check, allowing double bookings on override days
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 133-135), when `dateOverrideExist` is true and the slot falls within the date override window, the function immediately returns `true` without executing the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. As a result, any calendar busy times or existing Cal.com bookings on a date with a date override are completely ignored, causing already-booked or busy slots to be returned as available.

findings.title: Comparing two Dayjs objects with `===` is always false, breaking full-day unavailability overrides
findings.body: Line 114 checks `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` to detect an all-day unavailable override (where `start` and `end` are equal). Because `dayjs(...)` constructs a new object each time, `===` compares object references and always evaluates to `false` (and `slotEndTime` is never before/same as `start` while `slotStartTime` is only `isAfter` `end`, not `isSame`), so a slot starting at `date.start` is not rejected. Use `.isSame(...)` instead of `===`.

findings.title: Date override boundary check allows slots that partially overlap the start or end of the override
findings.body: Lines 117-125 reject a slot only when `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd` (overlap test instead of containment test). This means: (1) a slot that starts before the date override begins but ends after `overrideStart` is considered valid, (2) a slot that starts before `overrideEnd` but ends after `overrideEnd` is considered valid, and (3) a slot whose `slotStartTime` equals `overrideEnd` is also considered valid because `isAfter` is strict. To require the slot to be within the date override window, the rejection condition should be `slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart) || slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`.

findings.title: Working hours check rejects valid slots when a user has multiple working hour intervals on the same day and ignores slotEndTime
findings.body: In lines 138-151, `workingHours.find(...)` returns truthy (causing `checkIfIsAvailable` to return `false`) as soon as ANY workingHour entry for that weekday does not contain `slotStartTime`. If a user has split working hours on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, or hours split across UTC midnight), a slot in the second interval fails the check against the first interval and is rejected. Additionally, line 142 computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so a slot extending past the end of working hours is not caught, and when `slotStartTime` and `slotEndTime` cross UTC midnight (or on days with no matching `workingHour.days`), the check does not work as intended.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day and `utcOffset` calculation in `checkIfIsAvailable`
findings.body: In lines 106-127: (1) `dateOverrides.find(...)` rejects a slot if it is outside the first matching override for that date, even when the user has multiple date override ranges on the same day and the slot falls inside a second override range. (2) `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` on a `Date` object interprets `date.start`'s local wall-clock time in the server's timezone rather than UTC, and adding `utcOffset * -1` shifts a timestamp that was already converted to UTC by `getUserAvailability` back to organizer wall-clock time while `slotStartTime` is in real UTC (`time.utc()`), so comparing `slotStartTime` and `slotEndTime` against `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares UTC slot times against organizer-local override times whenever `organizerTimeZone` is not UTC.
